Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: Shared-memory keys are folded with `key % SHM_PAGE_NUM` and no key is stored, so distinct keys silently share one page
FILE: Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c
CLAIM: shm_page_get() (line 337) selects the descriptor with `&shm_page[(uint32_t)key % SHM_PAGE_NUM]` (SHM_PAGE_NUM = 100) and nothing anywhere records which key owns a slot; shm_page_t only holds {count, pa}. Two unrelated programs using keys that are congruent mod 100 — e.g. 42 (consensus's SHMP_KEY) and 142, or 7 and 107 — are handed the same physical frame and the same refcount, so each one sees the other's writes and either can trigger the count==0 free while the other is still attached. mm.c already owns the descriptor table, so a parallel `static int shm_key[SHM_PAGE_NUM];` plus a linear search for a matching-or-free slot (and clearing it when count hits 0 in shm_page_dt/free_process_user_page) removes the aliasing.

diff --git a/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h b/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h
index 59b44eb..ebd6999 100644
--- a/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h
+++ b/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h
@@ -102,6 +102,24 @@ extern unsigned long free_page_num();
 extern PTE* init_page_table();
 extern void free_process_user_page(PTE* pgdir);
 
+/* pgdir is pa. if va is not mapped, then map it. returns the kva of the page */
+extern uintptr_t alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir);
+extern PTE* find_pte(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir);
+
+/* user virtual address window reserved for shared pages: it stops right
+ * below the first page a user ELF is linked at (its headers live at 0xf000) */
+#define SHM_VA_BEGIN 0x1000lu
+#define SHM_VA_END   0xf000lu
+
+/* the image of a user program, headers included, and the first page of its
+ * stack are mapped when the address space is created */
+#define USER_CODE_BEGIN 0xf000lu
+#define USER_CODE_END   0x14000lu
+
+/* one 4KB page is eight 512 byte SD card blocks */
+#define SD_BLOCK_SIZE 512
+#define PAGE_SD_BLOCKS (PAGE_SIZE / SD_BLOCK_SIZE)
+
 uintptr_t shm_page_get(int key);
 extern void shm_page_dt(uintptr_t addr);

input.reason: REFUTED. (1) The keyless table is given, not new: `git show HEAD:Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h` proves `#define SHM_PAGE_NUM 100` and `typedef struct shm_page{int count; uintptr_t pa;}` (lines 79-84) are unchanged framework code; the new diff to that header only adds SHM_VA_BEGIN/END, USER_CODE_*, and SD-block macros at line 102+. A fixed 100-entry descriptor array with no key field encodes the contract 'key is the slot index, 0 <= key < 100'. Under that contract `key % SHM_PAGE_NUM` is the identity and is injective — no two valid keys alias. Dropping the modulo would make key >= 100 an out-of-bounds write into shm_page[], so the modulo is strictly a safety guard, not the source of a bug. (2) No reachable trigger: grepping test/, tiny_libc/, include/ shows the sole shm user in the tree is /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/test/consensus.c with `#define SHMP_KEY 42` (all 9 consensus processes use it); test_shell.c passes no key and no key ever originates from user input. No program uses 142, 107, or any key >= 100, so the 'two unrelated programs collide' scenario cannot occur. (3) The asserted harm is factually false: in /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c, `page->count++` happens exactly once per successful mapping in shm_page_get (line 355), and count is decremented exactly once per unmap in shm_page_dt (line 385) and free_process_user_page (line 303), both guarded by `shm_page[i].count > 0 && shm_page[i].pa == pa`. count is thus the additive total of live mappings across all processes and all keys landing in the slot, so count==0 implies zero live mappings and free_user_page(pa) can never run while another process is still attached — there is no premature free or use-after-free. Released slots also set pa = 0 while all lookups require count > 0, so no stale-pa aliasing either. The only conceivable effect is data sharing between two out-of-contract keys, which no code in the tree can produce.
